title: Structured Vocabulary
description: The structured vocabulary as neutral DATA (principle 5). The engine reads this file to know which commands exist and with which parameters (for tool calling); the add-on provides the IMPLEMENTATION in addon/ai_copilot/executor/vocabulary/. Adding a command = one entry here + one function in the executor. This is v0.1: a minimal catalog. Units are mm and degrees unless stated otherwise.

transaction_id.description: id of the undoable transaction the action ran within

created_ids.description: ids of the FreeCAD objects created/modified

recompute_ok.description: outcome of the recompute (input for the self-correction loop)

error.description: message when ok=false (e.g. geometrically impossible operation)

catalog._comment: Each command declares its parameters as a mini JSON Schema, so the engine can generate and validate them. Initial catalog; it grows phase by phase.

create_cone.summary: Create a cone (or a truncated cone). radius1 is the base radius; radius2 is the TOP radius (default 0 = pointed cone; give both for a frustum).

radius2.description: top radius in mm (default 0 = pointed tip)

create_torus.summary: Create a torus (a ring/donut). radius1 is the ring radius (centre of the tube to the axis); radius2 is the tube radius (must be smaller).

radius1.description: ring radius in mm (axis to tube centre)

revolve.summary: Revolve a sketch/profile around an axis to make a solid of revolution (e.g. a vase, a pulley). The target is usually the 'Sketch' made by create_sketch. angle defaults to 360 (full revolution); axis is 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' (default 'Z') passing through 'base' (default the origin). Give axes as letters, never as raw vectors.

target.description: id of the sketch/profile to revolve (e.g. 'Sketch')

base.description: [x,y,z] point the axis passes through, optional (default: the origin)

drill_hole.summary: Drill a cylindrical hole into an existing body.

target.description: id of the body to drill

create_sketch.summary: Create a 2D sketch (a real Sketcher sketch) to be turned into a solid with 'extrude', 'revolve', 'loft' or 'sweep'. Choose a 'shape' on a standard 'plane'. The new object is named 'Sketch'. Shapes: 'rectangle' (width+height), 'circle' (radius), 'polygon' (sides+radius), 'slot' = rounded slot (length+width), 'polyline' = closed wire through 'points'.

plane.description: reference plane the sketch lies on (default XY)

sides.description: polygon: number of sides (required when shape='polygon')

length.description: slot: OVERALL length, must be > width (required when shape='slot')

thickness.description: profile leg/ring thickness (required when shape='angle','L','tube' or 'rtube'); for tube must be < radius

web_thickness.description: T: web thickness (required when shape='T'); must be <= width

flange_thickness.description: T: flange thickness (required when shape='T'); must be <= height

points.description: polyline: at least 3 [x,y] pairs in mm; the wire closes automatically. A third number [x,y,bulge] makes the edge to the NEXT point an arc bulging by that height (positive = left)

placement.description: [x,y,z] origin offset, optional (use it to space loft profiles apart)

loft.summary: Loft a solid through 2+ profiles in order (e.g. a square that morphs into a circle). Draw each profile first with create_sketch (space them apart with 'placement'), then pass their names in 'profiles'; the tool links the real sketches automatically.

profiles.description: ordered list of at least 2 sketch/profile ids

solid.description: make a solid (default true); false = a hollow surface

ruled.description: straight-line transitions between profiles (default false = smooth)

sweep.summary: Sweep a profile along a path (e.g. a circle along a curved polyline = a pipe). Draw the PROFILE first, then the PATH (often a polyline sketch on a perpendicular plane), then sweep; the tool links the real sketches automatically.

path.description: id of the sketch/wire to sweep along

frenet.description: profile follows the path's curvature (default true)

shell.summary: Hollow a solid into a thin-walled shell, leaving one face OPEN (like a box without a lid). Pick the open face with 'where' ('top' or 'bottom'); the tool resolves the real face itself. thickness = wall thickness in mm; the walls grow inward, outer dimensions stay.

target.description: id of the solid to hollow

where.description: which face is left open (default top)

face.description: OPTIONAL explicit face id like 'Face3'; prefer 'where'

extrude.summary: Extrude a sketch/profile into a solid. The target is usually the 'Sketch' made by create_sketch or sketch_on_face. distance is the height; negative reverses, symmetric extrudes both ways. Set op='cut' to make a POCKET: the profile is pushed INTO the body it sits on and the material is removed (the sketch must be on a face, via sketch_on_face).

op.description: 'add' (default) makes a new solid; 'cut' makes a pocket by removing material from the body the sketch sits on

chamfer.summary: Bevel (chamfer) a body's edges. By default it chamfers ALL edges; set 'where' to pick a group, or list explicit 'edges' ids. You normally do NOT need to list edges.

target.description: id of the body to chamfer

where.description: which edges to chamfer when 'edges' is omitted (default: all). The tool resolves the real edges itself.

edges.description: OPTIONAL explicit edge ids (e.g. 'Edge3'); omit to use 'where' instead

fillet.summary: Round (fillet) a body's edges. By default it rounds ALL edges; set 'where' to pick a group, or list explicit 'edges' ids. You normally do NOT need to list edges.

target.description: id of the body to fillet

where.description: which edges to round when 'edges' is omitted (default: all). The tool resolves the real edges itself.

edges.description: OPTIONAL explicit edge ids (e.g. 'Edge3'); omit to use 'where' instead

move.summary: Move (translate) an existing object. Prefer 'by' [dx,dy,dz] for a relative move; use 'to' [x,y,z] for an absolute position. Reversible (changes the object's Placement). Units: mm.

target.description: id of the object to move

rotate.summary: Rotate an existing object around an axis by an angle in degrees. Reversible (changes the object's Placement). By default it rotates around Z through the object's centre.

target.description: id of the object to rotate

center.description: [x,y,z] pivot point, optional (default: the object's bounding-box centre)

mirror.summary: Mirror (reflect) an existing object across a standard plane, keeping the original. Creates a new mirrored copy. Give axes/planes as letters, never as raw vectors.

target.description: id of the object to mirror

plane.description: mirror plane (default YZ = mirror left/right across X)

base.description: [x,y,z] point the mirror plane passes through, optional (default: origin)

array.summary: Make a pattern of copies of an existing object. 'pattern' is 'linear' (a row) or 'polar' (around an axis). 'count' is the TOTAL number of items including the original. Linear needs 'spacing' and a 'direction'; polar needs an 'angle' and an 'axis'.

target.description: id of the object to copy

pattern.description: row of copies (linear) or copies around an axis (polar)

count.description: TOTAL number of items, the original included

spacing.description: distance between items in mm (required for linear)

direction.description: direction of the linear row (default X)

angle.description: total angle in degrees to spread polar copies over (default 360 = full circle)

axis.description: rotation axis for a polar pattern (default Z)

center.description: [x,y,z] point the polar axis passes through, optional (default: the file origin [0,0,0]). The items orbit THIS centre, not the object's own centre.

radius.description: polar only, optional: radius of the circle. If given, the items are placed on a circle of this radius around the centre; if omitted, they orbit at the object's current distance from the centre.

sketch_on_face.summary: Create a 2D sketch attached to a FLAT face of an existing object, ready to extrude (e.g. to add a boss or cut a pocket). Pick the face with 'where' ('top' or 'bottom'); the tool resolves the real face itself, so you do NOT guess a face number. Choose 'shape' ('rectangle' or 'circle'); a rectangle needs width and height, a circle needs radius. The new sketch is named 'Sketch'; extrude it next (use op='cut' for a pocket).

target.description: id of the object that owns the face

where.description: pick the face by position; the tool finds the real face index (default top)

face.description: OPTIONAL explicit face id like 'Face6'; prefer 'where' and let the tool resolve it

shape.description: profile to draw on the face

sides.description: polygon: number of sides (required when shape='polygon')

length.description: slot: OVERALL length, must be > width (required when shape='slot')

offset.description: optional gap between the face and the sketch, mm

place_on.summary: Place a part ON (rest on top of / below) another part's face, by reading the real geometry. The model says 'put the bracket on the base plate'; it does NOT compute where. Pick the face with 'face' (default top; or bottom/left/right/front/back). Only the target's position changes; keep its orientation (rotate it first if you need it turned).

target.description: id of the object to reposition

below.description: id of the object whose face the target rests on

face.description: which face of 'below' to rest on (default top)

gap.description: gap in mm between the target and the face (default 0 = touching)

mate.summary: Joint assembly: mate two parts so a face of one touches a face of the other, facing each other. General form of 'place_on' (which is the bottom-of-a-on-top-of-b special case). Give each part's face by name. With 'align' (default on), the tool also rotates the first part so its face points straight at the other; set align=false to only move it, keeping its current orientation.

a.description: id of the part to reposition

b.description: id of the part it mates against

gap.description: gap in mm between the two faces (default 0 = touching)

align.description: rotate 'a' so its face points at 'b' (default true; false = move only)

group.summary: Put several parts into a named group (a folder in the assembly tree). Reusing an existing group name adds to that group instead of making a new one. This is how an assembly is organised into a body hierarchy.

members.description: ids of the objects to include in the group

label.summary: Name a part (set its label) and, optionally, attach a note. Naming is the first step of MBD: every part in an assembly should have a clear name so the assembly tree, drawings and downstream tools can address it.

target.description: id of the object to label

label.description: the name/label to give the part

note.description: optional free-text note stored on the part (e.g. material, spec)
